question: A user request: "Use the tao-run-on-docker skill." Identify which TAO skill applies and, reading only that skill's documentation, outline the steps it prescribes. Do NOT run any commands, scripts, web searches, or other tools — describe the plan only.
ground_truth: Identify tao-run-on-docker as the applicable skill and summarize its documented workflow from SKILL.md without executing anything.
expected_behavior: Identifies tao-run-on-docker as the relevant skill
Outlines the documented workflow steps from SKILL.md
Does not run commands, scripts, or web searches

question: Using local Docker, run a short-lived container job end to end and report its final state: submit it, poll status, fetch the last lines of its logs, then cancel and tear it down. Use a tiny public image (e.g. busybox) — this checks the execution contract, not model training, so no GPU is required.
ground_truth: Load tao-run-on-docker and implement its four verbs against the local daemon: lint the command with redact_secrets.py, open a job record to mint JOB_ID BEFORE launching, name the container after JOB_ID so the later verbs can find it, mark RUNNING with the container id as backend-ref, map docker's native state to the fixed vocabulary, fetch logs by JOB_ID, then remove the container and mark the record CANCELED. Verified end to end against a live daemon.
expected_behavior: Opens the job record with tao_job_record.py BEFORE `docker run`, not after — the minted id is the only handle the launch can use
Names/labels the container after $JOB_ID so status, logs, and cancel can locate it
Marks RUNNING with --backend-ref set to the container id returned by `docker run -d`
Maps docker's native state to the fixed vocabulary (PENDING RUNNING COMPLETE ERROR CANCELED UNKNOWN) rather than reporting the raw string
Fetches logs by $JOB_ID rather than by a container id it kept in a shell variable
Removes the container and marks the record CANCELED — leaving a record in PENDING after a failed or finished run is a leak
Does not require a GPU, and does not pull a TAO image for a lifecycle check
